answer: To resist sybils, require every agent to forge a single bonded identity: lock a refundable stake that is slashed on proven fraud, and tie reputation to a pearl-like ledger of verifiable completed work that accrues slowly over time. New identities start with zero trust and earn capacity only through attested history, so flooding the ocean of agents with fresh clones costs real capital per clone while yielding no influence. Because stake and history cannot be copied, an attacker must pay full price for each fake identity, making large-scale fakery economically unviable.
